about.title: About Meenu Balaji, M.H.Sc- India's Leading Sports Nutritionist for Competitive Athletes
paragraphs: Meenu Balaji is one of India's leading sports nutritionists, specialising in performance nutrition for competitive and elite athletes across endurance, team, and strength sports.

With over 14 years of clinical and performance nutrition experience, Meenu has worked with swimmers, cricketers, track and field athletes, triathletes, and national-level competitors, building nutrition systems that hold up under the real demands of training camps, selection trials, multi-day tournaments, and international travel.

Her approach is built on three pillars that most sports nutrition practices in India don't offer together: evidence-based periodised nutrition, Indian food-first execution, and DNA-informed personalisation. This means every plan is grounded in sports science, practical for an Indian kitchen, and calibrated to your biology, not a template designed for a Western athlete eating foods you've never heard of.

Meenu holds advanced qualifications in sports nutrition and uses  DNA analyses in nutrition plans, one of a small number of nutrition professionals in India integrating genetic data into athletic performance planning.
She consults with athletes in Chennai and online across India, and has supported competitors preparing for national championships, international tours, and Olympic pathway programmes.
If you are looking for a sports nutritionist in India who understands what elite competition actually demands, physically, logistically, and nutritionally, this is that practice.

faqs.question: What should I eat before a workout or game?
paragraphs: Focus on easily digestible carbs for energy (e.g., bananas, oatmeal, or whole-grain bread) and a small amount of protein to support muscles. Eat 2-3 hours before exercise.

faqs.question: What’s the best post-workout recovery meal?
paragraphs: A combination of protein (for muscle repair) and carbohydrates (to replenish glycogen) is ideal—examples include a protein shake with fruit or chicken with rice and vegetables.

faqs.question: How much protein do athletes need?
paragraphs: Protein requirements vary by sport and training intensity but generally range from 1.2–2.0 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight daily.

faqs.question: How do I stay hydrated during sports?
paragraphs: Drink water regularly and consume electrolytes during prolonged activities (over an hour) to replace lost sodium, potassium, and magnesium.

faqs.question: How important is meal timing for athletes?
paragraphs: Timing meals and snacks around workouts is crucial. Eating carbs and protein before and after exercise can optimize energy, recovery, and muscle repair.

faqs.question: What does a DNA-informed sports nutrition plan include?
paragraphs: Most athletes follow nutrition advice built for a statistical average. DNA-informed sports nutrition replaces that average with your actual biology.

A genetic assessment looks at the markers most relevant to athletic performance, how your body oxidises fat versus carbohydrate during exercise, your muscle fibre composition and recovery profile, your inflammatory and injury risk, your power and endurance genetic predispositions, and how efficiently you absorb and use nutrients like iron, Vitamin D, B12, and caffeine.

This data is then layered into your performance nutrition plan. So rather than following a standard high-carbohydrate endurance protocol because that is what most plans recommend, your plan is built around whether your genetics support that approach, or whether a different macro distribution would serve your body and your sport better. It is the difference between a plan that is generally correct and one that is correct for you.

faqs.question: How is sports nutrition different for elite athletes versus recreational athletes?
paragraphs: Recreational athletes benefit from general healthy eating principles. Elite athletes require periodised nutrition, meaning intake, macro ratios, and timing shift deliberately across training blocks, taper weeks, competition days, and recovery phases. The margin for error is smaller, the stakes are higher, and the plan needs to hold up across travel, tournaments, and high training loads.

faqs.question: Do you provide nutrition support for Ironman and triathlon training?
paragraphs: Yes. We build periodised plans for long-course triathlon covering fueling across swim-bike-run training blocks, brick-session nutrition, carb loading, race-day fueling strategy, and heat-adjusted hydration, so your nutrition scales with training volume and holds up on race day.
